title: One owned thing: Tämä on …
summary: Identify one owned thing with Tämä on and the already learned owner endings.
objectives: Identify one owned thing with Tämä on and the already learned owner endings.
Apply this rule with the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Tämä means “this”, on means “is”: Tämä on identifies one thing. Put the owner phrase after that frame.
Tämä on meidän pallomme means “This is our ball.” Use the endings already learned: meidän (“our”) selects -mme; teidän (“your”) selects -nne; heidän (“their”) selects -nsa.
The thing being identified determines on or ovat. Even when several people own one ball, the one-ball frame remains Tämä on. Tasks show whether one person or a group is addressed as “you”.
keyPoints: Identify one owned thing with Tämä on and the already learned owner endings.

steps: Tämä on (“This is”) identifies one thing.
Tämä on (“This is”) identifies one thing.
Tämä on (“This is”) identifies one thing.

commonMistakes: Use on for one thing, regardless of owner number.
Keep the noun ending after the personal owner.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Write “This is your apple.” in Finnish. Begin with Tämä on. Address a group. Use omena (“apple”).
practiceExercises.explanation: Tämä on identifies one thing. The ending -nne identifies your ownership.
practiceExercises.misconceptionCategory: Simple ownership identity sentences: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.pattern: demonstrative + agreeing olla + optional owner pronoun + possessed noun

parts.formation: Use on with one thing, independently of how many people own it.
Teidän is the personal owner form of te; it selects -nne.
omena (“apple”) + -nne = omenanne. The same possessed form can name one or several things; this sentence names one.

answerDiagnostics.explanation: Drop the noun’s plural -t before -nne: use omenanne.
Keep the possessive ending -nne even when the owner pronoun is present or omitted.
Teidän needs -nne; changing the ending changes the owner.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Build “This is their house.” Begin with Tämä on. Keep heidän.
practiceExercises.explanation: Tämä on identifies one thing. The ending -nsa identifies their ownership.

parts.formation: Use on with one thing, independently of how many people own it.
Heidän is the personal owner form of he; it selects -nsa.
talo (“house”) + -nsa = talonsa. The same possessed form can name one or several things; this sentence names one.

practiceExercises.explanation: Tämä on means “This is”. The noun ending marks the owner; the demonstrative and verb reveal the number of things.
